questions.subject: chemistry
questions.content:
Match the compounds in Column I with their characteristic test(s)/reaction(s) given in Column II. Indicate your answer by darkening the appropriate bubbles of the 4 4 matrix given in the ORS.

Column I Column II
(A) (P) sodium fusion extract of the compound gives Prussian blue colour with FeSO.
(B) (Q) gives positive FeCl test.
(C) (R) gives white precipitate with AgNO.
(D) (S) reacts with aldehydes to form the corresponding hydrazone derivative.

questions.explanation:
A, B, C, D will give NaCN in their sodium fusion extract. Adding FeSO will give Fe[Fe(CN)] which is Prussian blue in colour.

B and C have Phenol group which gave positive result to FeCl test.

A, B, C, D both give precipitate with AgNO but only A and C will give pure white precipitate.

A and D can only give hydrazone derivative in reaction with aldehyde.
